Issued at 412 AM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Pattern amplification well underway over the CONUS...with western 
ridge building up into Alberta/Saskatchewan on the nose of a 140kt 
upper jet...and longwave troughing settling back into the eastern US 
(particularly, the Midwest), blocked from eastward motion by ridging 
over the north Atlantic; 100kt meridional jet diving down through 
the Plains attm as the thermal gradient aloft tightens. Lobes of PV 
digging into the Midwest attm. Pacific moisture still funneling 
northward into the Canadian Rockies...and over the ridge and 
into the Plains...with deepest moisture over the SE US ahead of 
the trough axis...though pwats are a little better over the OH 
Valley ahead of a notable PV max there. Pool of cold air to our 
north (-12C at 850mb over western Ontario) being advected 
southward on generally N to NE winds in the low levels; 
trajectories suggest the coldest air will funnel around northern
MI (as usual), though our temps aloft are dropping, with the 0C
850mb line now well south across southern Lower MI. At the 
surface...1032mb cold surface high over northern 
Manitoba...1003mb surface low over the central OH Valley with 
cold front draped back to TX...and baroclinic zone stretching 
from British Columbia to MO. Indications of an inverted trough 
over NE MI attm, with a subtle surface low over the St. Mary's 
River system and a subtle cold front stretching down into NW MI 
(where a slow moving band of rainfall has been all 
evening...though it is beginning to move a bit quicker as of 6z 
as upstream PV max digs in. 

Multiple lobes of energy to dive into the Midwest over the next 
couple days, reinforcing the idea of troughing and cool/unsettled 
weather over the Great Lakes (including snow at times)...though the 
center of the upper low looks to remain to our east for now. Ridging 
will slowly press in this weekend ahead of another couple punches of 
energy being thrown into the West Coast, though some influences of 
the departing trough may hang on into the weekend regardless of high 
pressure. Appears some of this West Coast energy will plow its way 
across the base of the ridge, through the central/southern US...as 
northern piece rides overtop the ridge through central Canada Sunday 
into Monday. Additional energy digging into the western US early-mid 
week will build ridging over the Midwest again...with signals for 
energy to try to progress eastward into the central Plains toward 
the end of the period. At the very least...anticipate high pressure 
will eventually give way to return flow into the Upper Midwest, and 
may need to keep an eye out for some active weather going into the 
middle-end of next week.

FORECAST DETAILS...

Snow accumulations tonight...Signals now point toward a more NE flow 
tonight, rather than the N flow it had been signaling earlier. This 
still suggests convergence will be enhanced by Grand Traverse Bay, 
particularly noting that the south end of the Bay(s) have a slight 
SSW-NNE orientation...and should still lead to some upslope 
enhancement toward the higher terrain west of TC into Leelanau
county...as well as down toward 
Interlochen/Thompsonville/Buckley. Think another potential 
maximum for precip will be from Northport down to Manistee, with
more snow accumulation potential in the higher elevations 
between those two areas...though it is possible the QPF bullseye
could remain just offshore, especially if flow weakens enough 
inland to allow for a subtle land breeze to develop. With lake 
temperatures still running around 10-12C, do wonder how close to
the coast snow will fall, let alone accumulate...though a more 
easterly component could potentially limit the lake influence on
temps and keep things a touch cooler in the coastal areas. 
Localized QPF bullseyes could be as high as 0.50-0.70 overnight,
which, even with sloppy snow-to- liquid ratios around 5:1 or 
less, suggests potential for a couple inches of snow could fall,
if not more...though question still remains if it will be able 
to stick around given the warm soil temps (still 47F at the MSU 
extension research center in Leelanau County). However, still 
have concerns that convection could be vigorous enough to 
overwhelm the warm surface temps and accumulate anyway. Current 
forecast has an inch or two total for tonight, focused 
particularly over the Leelanau Peninsula, which seems reasonable
attm. Think snow (or at least, mix showers) will continue into 
the morning hours until deeper moisture departs. 

There are also some increasing signals for lake effect off Lake 
Huron into NE Lower MI, which makes sense given more of a NE flow in 
the lower levels. Fetch will not be quite as maximized over here as 
for points along the coast of Lake MI (except for perhaps areas 
toward Harrisville and south)...and the lake surface temps are a 
little cooler over here than on the west side (closer to 10C vs 
closer to 12C, respectively).
